WHY YOU LOSE THE ONES YOU SHOULD WIN

Three trucks.
One driveway.

A homeowner books three estimates. All three companies are licensed, all three are insured, all three have four and a half stars and a page of four sentence reviews. Nothing on the table tells them apart except the number at the bottom.

The thing that actually separates you happened on somebody else’s job. The crew that found the real problem behind the wall. The install your lead tech would not sign off until it was right. The homeowner who tells everyone at church about you.

None of that leaves the house. We go and get it, and put it where the decision gets made.

SOUND FAMILIAR?

Common problems we see

01

Price is the only difference

When a homeowner cannot see a difference, they pick the cheapest number on the kitchen table. You lose jobs to people who do worse work.

02

Reviews do all the selling

Five stars and four sentences, on the same platform as everybody else. A homeowner spending fifteen thousand dollars wants more than that.

03

The work disappears

The best thing you did is behind drywall, under shingles or in a crawl space by Friday. Nobody will ever see it again.

04

Nobody wants the job

You are short installers every season, and your careers page has a photo of a truck that is not yours on it.

WHAT YOU GET

One install, three pieces,
one link you can text.

01

The homeowner film.

Two to three minutes. The customer saying what was wrong, what you did and what it is like now, in their own house, in their own words. Not a review. A story with a face on it, and your crew in the background actually working.

02

The social cuts.

Five social cuts, fifteen to forty-five seconds, captioned and ready to post. Before we film we agree the five things the content has to fix: the objection that kills your close rate, the question every homeowner asks, the role you cannot fill. Every cut answers one of them.

03

The project page.

A written case study at a link that is yours. The house, the problem, what you found, what you did and what the homeowner said. Text it after the estimate. Put it on the quote. Run it as the landing page for your ads.

BUILT AROUND YOUR CREW

A plan, a day, and we handle the rest.

You are running installs, not a production. The plan is agreed before we film, so nothing comes back that you cannot use.

01

We pick the job before we film it.

We go through your recent work and choose the install worth showing, then name the problems the content has to solve. Every deliverable is mapped to one of them before a camera comes out of the case.

02

We ask the homeowner, not you.

We handle the call, the release and the scheduling. If they say no we pick another job. Your office does not chase anything.

03

One day on the install.

We work around your crew. Nobody stops working, nobody has to perform, and we bring our own insurance certificates and boot covers.

04

Then we do the rest.

We interview, edit, write and build the page. You approve it once, in one place.

First cut in fourteen days. If it is late, you do not pay.The clock pauses while we wait on your approvals.

THE DEADLINE

On Friday it is just a finished house.

The proof is the work, and the work only exists while it is happening. Once the crew packs up and the drywall goes back, no version of this can be recovered. Not at any price, not by anyone.

If there is an install running this week that you would want a homeowner to see, that is the one.

TERMS

The things we guarantee.

First cut in fourteen days or you do not pay.

Fourteen days after we leave the job, the first cut is in your hands. A day late and the project is free and you keep everything. Only that first cut carries a date, and its clock pauses on your approvals.

We work around your crew, not the other way around.

A full day on the job, on your schedule. We bring our own insurance certificates, PPE and boot covers, and nobody gets pulled off the install to stand in front of a camera.

If the footage is not right, we come back on our dime.

If what we got does not hold up, we book another day and cover it. No change order, no trip charge.

QUESTIONS

A few things worth knowing.

What if the homeowner will not go on camera?

Then we pick a different job, and it costs you nothing. We make the ask ourselves, before the shoot is scheduled, so a no is a scheduling note rather than a wasted day. Most people say yes when the work went well and somebody asks properly.

Does the house have to be finished?

No, and the best ones usually are not. Half the story is the problem you found, so we want the attic, the crawl space and the panel while they are still open.

Why is the price the same for every client?

Because the deliverables are. Custom scopes are why other vendors take three weeks to send you a proposal.

Can I upgrade after the shoot?

Yes. We capture everything on the day regardless of package. Add the social cuts or the written assets within thirty days of the shoot at the difference in price. An Install Day upgrades the same way, with the full $1,500 coming off.

What is the difference between video plus written and video only?

Video only is the films on their own. Video plus written adds the project page and its one page version for the quote, written from the same interviews. Same day on the job either way.

Do you need my techs on camera?

One or two, for a few minutes each, and only if they are willing. The homeowner carries the story. Your crew is what makes it look like a company somebody would want to work for.

Do you work outside Central Ohio?

Yes. Central Ohio work is filmed by our local crew with no travel costs. Elsewhere we send a vetted crew from our network, directed by us, with the same deliverables and the same fourteen day guarantee. Travel is quoted at cost.

What if the weather turns?

We reschedule at no charge and the clock starts from the new date.

Who owns the footage?

You do. Your organized raw archive is included in every package, and the homeowner release covers your own marketing use.
